newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker looks at new deepwater rig concept.
newsitem.headline: Aker looks at new deepwater rig concept.

text.p: Norwegian offshore and engineering group Aker ASA said on Wednesday it was developing a new type of drilling rig to operate in 3,000 metres of water.
The rig, based on a Spar sub-structure, is being developed in cooperation with J. Ray McDermott for Shell Offshore in the U.S.
A Spar sub-structure comprises a cylinder floating vertically in the water to support the topsides.

Aker said the design work would be completed by the end of the year. Detailed engineering and construction of the first unit could begin in 1997 for completion two years later, the company said in its weekly Aker Pulse newsletter.

Aker said Shell was considering chartering the rig for three years to drill deepwater wells in the Gulf of Mexico. Shell also has an option to hire two similar units, and charter terms will be clarified over the next few months, Aker said.
"We'll take a stake in the first of these rigs in order to commercialise this new and highly promising concept," said Svein Eggen, president of Aker Oil and Gas Technology.
Aker said McDermott would take a stake in the unit and a third party could also become involved.
